builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
summary: Bonbon replaces structure-dependent molecular interaction pipelines (co-folding, docking-based binding-site and affinity prediction, and task-specific supervised models) with zero-shot inference from a frozen protein-ligand sequence foundation model. The cost is dependence on a 1.6B-parameter pretrained model the reader cannot train themselves, plus validation overhead to confirm emergent capabilities transfer to their specific targets; inference itself is lightweight and API-compatible. It can fail on molecular series far from the training distribution, emergent capabilities may not transfer to novel protein families, and the model offers no structural coordinates when atom-level pose information is required.
rationale: The reader cannot train a 1.6B-parameter model on 3.2T paired tokens, but if Bonbon or its frozen embeddings are accessible via release or API, adopting them for zero-shot binding-site, mechanism-of-action, and affinity inference could replace costly structure-based pipelines on a single 24GB GPU; otherwise it remains observational until weights or a service become available.

claims.statement: Bonbon replaces structure-dependent molecular interaction pipelines (co-folding, docking-based binding-site and affinity prediction, and task-specific supervised models) with zero-shot inference from a frozen protein-ligand sequence foundation model. The cost is dependence on a 1.6B-parameter pretrained model the reader cannot train themselves, plus validation overhead to confirm emergent capabilities transfer to their specific targets; inference itself is lightweight and API-compatible. It can fail on molecular series far from the training distribution, emergent capabilities may not transfer to novel protein families, and the model offers no structural coordinates when atom-level pose information is required.

Frozen Bonbon representations achieve state-of-the-art binding and affinity prediction at five orders of magnitude greater speed than co-folding methods, with a 61.5% dose-response hit rate in prospective wet-lab validation across nine disease targets.
